docs.text: you want to… see copy-paste one page and run it Quickstart decide which model to run Choose a method handle roles, trios, real tables Data preparation estimate a CIP — Kaplan–Meier, Aalen–Johansen (use III may stop here) CIP estimation pick an engine, scale up, export to a GWAS Estimation fit \(h^2\) or \(A{+}C{+}M\) Inference run the pre-flight list Assumptions & checklist see measured accuracy, speed and failure modes Benchmark results read the maths behind equation (1) Algorithm read the methods note (same I/II/III) Technical report

docs.title: Independent review of ltpred v0.3.4 (2026-08)
docs.text:
Historical document

This review audits v0.3.4 at commit cf8cc99. It predates the 0.4.0 lean-down, so some machinery it checks (for example scripts/check_results.py) no longer exists, and its findings have since been addressed or superseded. Kept for provenance; do not read it as a description of the current release.

A read-only, peer-review-style audit of the statistical core, the estimation and fitting APIs, the supporting numerics, the test and CI machinery, the benchmark evidence base, the documentation, and the literature positioning. This review covers the tree at commit cf8cc99 (v0.3.4); it follows, and is independent of, the archived v0.3.0 review in EXTERNAL_REVIEW.md. No files were modified by the review.

docs.title: 1. Scope and method
docs.text:
The review proceeded in three stages. First, the project's own gates were run: the full test suite, the linter, the evidence guards, and a strict documentation build (Table 1). Second, seven areas were reviewed in parallel against the primary sources: the code, docs/algorithm.md, the benchmark artifacts in benchmarks/, and the published literature. Third, every finding reported here at tiers T1 and T2 was re-verified independently against the code or the artifacts — each number quoted below was recomputed from the committed CSVs or reproduced by execution. Severity tiers: T1, correctness or scientific validity; T2, robustness, evidence integrity, or maintainability; T3, style, clarity, or polish.

Table 1. Baseline checks run on the review machine (macOS, Apple silicon; conda env ltpred314: CPython 3.14.6 free-threading, NumPy 2.4.6, SciPy 1.18.0, Numba 0.66.0, pytest 9.1.1, ruff 0.16.1).

Check Command Result Test suite pytest -q (tests + research) 714 passed, 1 skipped, 196 s Lint ruff check . clean Evidence guards scripts/check_results.py 83/83 guards ok Docs mkdocs build --strict (isolated venv, mkdocs-material ≥ 9) builds clean

The one local caveat: no conda env on the machine has mkdocs installed, so scripts/check_docs.py fails at its anchor half with "No module named mkdocs". The strict build itself passes in an isolated venv; the guard failure is an environment gap, not a documentation defect. (check_docs.py failing hard when mkdocs is absent is arguably correct behaviour for a guard.)

docs.title: 2. Verdicts by area
docs.text:
Statistical core (covariance.py, thresholds.py, pearson_aitken.py, gibbs.py). Correct. The bound conventions (case/control orientation, onset pins, interval censoring), the Pearson–Aitken rank-1 update, the censoring-mixture weights, the precision-form Gibbs full conditionals, and the new collapsed sweep were verified against docs/algorithm.md eqs. (1)–(11), against closed-form truncated-normal conditionals, and against scipy.stats.truncnorm/high-precision references, including the far-tail regimes (|z| ≈ 38.5 handoff) and near-degenerate intervals. Kinship coefficients, the tabular method (including inbreeding), and the PD correction were checked on hand-built pedigrees. Cross-engine agreement on probe families matches within Monte-Carlo error.

Estimation and fitting (estimate.py, fit.py, simulate.py). Sound. The LiabilityResult separation of Monte-Carlo SE (se, shrinks with draws) from posterior variance (var, does not) is the statistically right bookkeeping and is documented candidly. The contract gates (multi-trait vs c2/m2, Gibbs vs mixture) behave as documented with no silently-accepting path found. The IPW construction is a correct Horvitz–Thompson weighting over families, and the case-rate screen, the Haseman–Elston-type fixed-point fitter, and the family-cluster bootstrap all match their documentation. The three onset models in simulate.py were verified numerically against their specification.

Supporting numerics (cip.py, tetrachoric.py, liability_scale.py, _mathfun.py, _numba.py, pedigree.py, family.py). Correct where it matters. Kaplan–Meier and Aalen–Johansen estimates and their Greenwood/Aalen standard errors match R survival/cmprsk to all printed digits under ties, delayed entry, and risk-set exhaustion; the tetrachoric MLE matches polycor to ~1e-5; the Lee et al. liability-scale transforms round-trip exactly; AS 241 matches scipy.special.ndtri to 6e-16 relative error down to p = 1e-300; the Numba JIT kernels are bit-identical to the pure-Python fallback.

Tests and CI. The oracle quality is high: closed forms, locked R outputs, and machine-precision kernel checks, with justified tolerances and disciplined seeding. The guard machinery genuinely recomputes from artifacts (no circularity found). Gaps are in CI coverage and in one vacuous research test (F2), plus the absence of a build/packaging leg and of an R-lock regression fixture (F15, F16).

Evidence base. Strong and honest in the main. All load-bearing guarded claims recompute exactly from the committed artifacts (83/83 guards), nearly every headline number carries the right kind of uncertainty (Monte-Carlo SE vs sampling variability is separated explicitly and repeatedly), and the interpretation is restrained — the λ_GC = 16.46 result is framed as a deliberate confounding demonstration, NCP claims carry their independent-SNP marginal-association simulation regime (not real-LD mixed-model evidence), and speedups carry their thread count. The defects found are one stale superlative (F1), a few last-digit/ordering transcription slips in unguarded prose (F7, F8, F17), and provenance gaps concentrated in the pre-schema-3 history (F9, F10).

Documentation. Accurate against the code: every documented parameter name and default checked matched; the quickstart executes verbatim; the equations and Algorithms G/P/M match the implementations step for step. Two numerical claims in the docs lack artifacts (F11, F12).

Literature positioning. Fair and accurate. Every load-bearing citation was verified against the publisher record — Pedersen et al. 2022 (AJHG 109:417–432, LT-FH++), Pedersen et al. 2023 (Nat Commun 14:5553, ADuLT), Dybdahl Krebs et al. 2024 (AJHG 111:2494–2509, PA-FGRS), Hujoel et al. 2020 (Nat Genet 52:541–547, LT-FH), Hujoel et al. 2022 (Cell Genomics 2:100152), and the forward-looking Dybdahl Krebs et al. 2026 (AJHG 113:184–201, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2025.11.016 — confirmed real; the 2025 in the DOI is the epub year). No misattribution: PA is consistently credited to Krebs et al. 2024, and the repo even reports Hujoel 2020's unfavourable PA comparison rather than cherry-picking. CITATION.cff is correct entry by entry. The defects are cosmetic (F33–F35).

docs.title: 3. Findings
docs.text:
Table 2. T1 findings (correctness / scientific validity). Both are narrow; neither indicts a published headline conclusion beyond the sentence quoted.

# Location Finding Evidence Recommended action F1 benchmarks/RESULTS.md:60-61; report/ltpred_methods.tex:665 The headline "stressful-pedigree benchmark remains at least 0.9984" is not supported by its artifact — and is contradicted by §14 of the same document ("worst single-seed … 0.99813", line 488). bench_pa_robustness.csv rare-K (K=0.005) per-seed agreements: 0.998429, 0.998131, 0.998225 → min 0.998131, mean 0.998262 (recomputed; regime means in the §14 table reproduce exactly). The error traces to the run log printing only the first seed (PA<->Gibbs=0.9984). No guard covers this figure. (The 0.9984 in paper/tables/accuracy_grid.* is a different, legitimate artifact.) Correct the headline to "at least 0.9981" (or quote 0.99813 worst-seed) in both files; add a guard recomputing min/mean regime agreement from the CSV. F2 research/tests/test_pipeline.py:119-129 test_stratified_cips_run_and_differ cannot fail under a wrong implementation: its only assertion is np.isfinite(out.est[0]), so an implementation that silently ignored cip_by_stratum would pass. This is the only test of the strata path. Read directly; the sibling test at lines 106–116 (test_censoring_changes_the_estimate) shows the intended "must differ" pattern. Assert the stratified estimate differs from the unstratified one (or equals a hand-computed two-curve reference).

Table 3. T2 findings (robustness, evidence integrity, maintainability).

# Location Finding Evidence Recommended action F3 ltpred/family.py:96-100 NaN fam_id silently fragments records into singleton "families": each NaN key compares unequal to itself, so grouping produces one family per NaN row. In a registry pipeline, missing IDs thus become relative-less estimates without any signal. Reproduced: fam_id=[1.0, nan, nan, 1.0] yields 3 families (two singleton NaN families), not 2 or an error. Reject non-finite fam_id in families_from_columns with a clear error. F4 ltpred/estimate.py:669-688 (_align_to_cov) The biobank-scale array APIs never check n_columns == len(roles): extra columns are silently ignored; short inputs fail with a raw IndexError. A mis-packed column matrix yields silently wrong liability scores on exactly the path where packing errors are most likely. Code read: columns are mapped purely by role-name index; agent's live repro: a 5-column bounds matrix with 3 roles returns an estimate from the first 3 columns without complaint. Add shape == (F, len(roles)) checks in _pa_from_role_arrays / _gibbs_from_role_arrays. F5 ltpred/_validation.py:22-46, ltpred/gibbs.py:744-746 Coincident infinite bounds (lower == upper == ±inf) pass validation and yield NaN Gibbs draws, propagating a NaN posterior mean. Unreachable from the threshold helpers (prevalences are confined to (0,1)), hence T2. Reproduced: rtmvnorm_gibbs(np.eye(1), [inf], [inf], seed=1) returns all-NaN with only a RuntimeWarning. Reject coincident non-finite bounds in validate_bounds. F6 ltpred/estimate.py:929-946 estimate_liability_from_kinship returns (est, var) under PA but (est, se) under Gibbs — the second positional element changes statistical meaning (posterior variance vs Monte-Carlo SE, >100× different in magnitude) with method. The Gibbs branch computes var and discards it (_var, line 944). Disclosed in the docstring, but it invites exactly the confusion LiabilityResult was built to prevent. Code read; agent verified the magnitude gap live (0.2882 vs 0.0017 on the same pedigree). Return (est, se, var) from both branches, or return a LiabilityResult-like object. F7 benchmarks/RESULTS.md:101, 561-564; README.md:229 Sex-CIP gap-closure quoted as 0.05091 ± 0.00096 and female shift as −0.03689; the artifact gives −0.0509182 ± 0.000958 and −0.036906 ± 0.000405, which round to 0.05092 and −0.03691. Wrong in the last quoted digit; unguarded. Recomputed from the paired-contrast row and independently re-paired from the 5 replicate rows (identical). Fix the digits in the three locations; extend check_results.py to the sex-isolation contrast rows. F8 benchmarks/RESULTS.md:77-81 The "respectively" clause misattributes peak RSS: the sentence order (LTFHPlus, ltpred Gibbs, LTFGRS PA, ltpred PA) maps 259.8 MiB to ltpred Gibbs and 165.3 to LTFGRS PA; the artifact says the reverse. (The §30 table is correct.) Recomputed from bench_ltfhplus_compare.csv: LTFHPlus 442.3, LTFGRS PA 259.8, ltpred Gibbs 165.3, ltpred PA 147.9 MiB. Reorder the prose or the numbers. F9 benchmarks/run_manifest.jsonl Provenance gaps. (a) Four committed CSVs — bench_pgs_comparison.csv, bench_pedigree_inference.csv, bench_register_pipeline.csv, bench_ascertainment_h2null.csv — have no manifest entry recording their production. (b) 40 of 44 recorded runs are schema-2 dirty-tree entries whose tracked_diff_sha256 hashes a diff whose content is not retained; only the 4 schema-3 runs of 2026-08-15 have recoverable source snapshots. Parsed all 44 manifest entries; zero changed_artifacts hits for the four CSVs. RESULTS.md's "Provenance limit" bullet partially discloses (b). Re-run the four artifacts through run_benchmark.py on a clean tree (or document the regeneration); state in RESULTS.md that schema-2 source state is unrecoverable. F10 benchmarks/RESULTS.md:158-161 The §2 sentence "system processes held 1-minute load average near 7–11 throughout" describes the superseded 2026-08-01 run (recorded 6.67 → 10.92), not the canonical 2026-08-15 run that produced the committed bench_scaling.csv (recorded 2.56 → 5.86). Benign direction — the canonical run was quieter than claimed. Manifest load_average fields for both runs (quoted). Update the sentence to the canonical run's recorded load. F11 docs/inference.md:213-216 The "≈0.97 cross-setting correlation" (scores correlated across an assumed-h² grid) has no artifact: bench_calibration.py computes only corrcoef(est, true_g); no committed benchmark computes the cross-setting correlation. The qualitative claim (ranking robust, scale fragile) is supported by §12; the number is not. Read the benchmark; repo-wide search for the computation finds nothing. Add the cross-setting correlation to bench_calibration.py/§12 with a guard, or reword to cite §12's corr-stability (0.429–0.431) and slope sweep without the 0.97 figure. F12 docs/algorithm.md:580-583 "Both identities above are verified numerically to Monte-Carlo precision (… four settings … recovered to ~1e-3)" — no such four-setting verification exists in tests/, benchmarks/, or scripts/. What exists (§28) verifies the correlation identity at CI half-width 0.016, and never tests the R²_joint identity. Repo-wide search for the verification code finds nothing; §28 numbers recomputed (observed 0.2009 ± 0.0046 vs theory 0.2003 ± 0.0050). Reword to cite §28 at its actual precision, and either add the small four-setting check as a test/benchmark or drop the claim for R²_joint. F13 .github/workflows/ci.yml:92-109 The oldest-deps job installs without numba and then runs the entire tests/ suite (524 tests), including all 12 jit_required tests and the sampling-heavy fit tests — plausibly 1–3+ hours per push, contradicting the marker's stated policy ("too sampling-heavy to run without the Numba JIT"). Read ci.yml; agent measured test_variance_components_recovers_A_and_C at 7.4 s with numba vs >300 s without. Add -m "not jit_required" and/or reuse the no-numba job's kernel-file list, keeping a small seeded subset for floor-version coverage. F14 .github/workflows/ci.yml:16-21; pyproject.toml classifiers Declared support (3.9–3.13, unbounded >=3.9, "OS Independent") exceeds tested coverage: 3.10/3.11 never run; no 3.14 or free-threaded leg although the project's own benchmark environment is CPython 3.14.6 free-threading (and the free-threading-sensitive code — thread-local seed streams, prange — is exactly what it would exercise); Windows untested. Read both files; benchmark env from run_manifest.jsonl. Add 3.10/3.11 (cheap) and one 3.14t leg if 3.14 is de-facto supported, or cap/document support. F15 .github/workflows/ci.yml No packaging/build verification anywhere: tests run from the source tree (pythonpath = ["."]), and no job builds an sdist/wheel. A broken distribution (dropped py.typed, omitted module, version = {attr} failure) would not be caught. Read ci.yml (6 jobs: test, research, lint, test-no-numba, oldest-deps, examples, docs). Add a python -m build + install-from-wheel + smoke-import job. F16 benchmarks/bench_ltfhplus_compare.csv; ci.yml The R lock (corr 0.9999 vs LTFHPlus 2.2.0; RMSE 0.000087 vs LTFGRS 1.0.1) exists only as a committed artifact: the R scripts are never run in CI and no pytest re-verifies the port against R output. A numerical regression in the Python port would pass the whole suite as long as nobody re-runs the benchmark. Defensible (R in CI is heavy) but should be a stated residual risk. Read ci.yml; the lock scripts are opt-in. Commit a small locked R-output fixture (a few dozen families) and assert reproduction within tolerance in pytest.

Table 4. T3 findings (style, clarity, polish). Locations verified against the tree unless noted.

# Location Finding Recommended action F17 README.md:87-88; docs/algorithm.md:820-822 "Both engines had correlation 0.9999 with the R Gibbs scores (RMSE 0.0041)": 0.0041 is the Gibbs figure (recomputed 0.004136); PA vs LTFHPlus is 0.0046 (recomputed 0.004621). Quote both RMSEs or drop the parenthetical. F18 ltpred/estimate.py:295-330 Batch-means SE divides by all retained draws (total_n += n_sim) while the batches cover only nb*b ≤ n_sim of them; R's batchmeans::bmmat (the cited source) uses n = a*b. SE understated by √(nb·b/n_sim): 0.07% at the default n_sim=100k, ~5% at n_sim=10. Use nb*b per round in the SE denominator. F19 ltpred/estimate.py:949-1011 Gibbs-only controls (tol, n_sim, burn_in, max_rounds, seed) are accepted but silently ignored on the default PA path; only seed carries a note. One docstring sentence, or a warning when non-default values meet the PA engine. F20 ltpred/estimate.py:1000 np.ndim(h2) > 0 routes any non-scalar h2 — including length-1 — into the multi-trait branch, yielding a confusing "needs genetic_corrmat" error for a numerically single-trait request. Treat size-1 h2 as scalar, or special-case the message. F21 ltpred/simulate.py:336-352 case_encoding="pin" is accepted with onset_model="stochastic"/"liability_dependent", fabricating liability information the generating process does not contain (acknowledged in a code comment; defaults are correct). Warn when "pin" combines with a non-threshold-crossing onset model. F22 ltpred/tetrachoric.py:147-149 The reported SE inverts the observed information with thresholds fixed at the marginal estimates (a few-percent understatement; 94% empirical nominal-95 coverage in the agent's 200-replicate probe), and the Wald form degrades near ρ F23 ltpred/cip.py:149 vs 219 aalen_johansen_cip requires integer-dtype event_type while kaplan_meier_cip accepts float 0/1 arrays — an inconsistency users hit when switching estimators on float-loaded registry columns. Accept integral float arrays in AJ, or document the asymmetry. F24 ltpred/pedigree.py:154 int(max_degree) silently truncates a non-integer (2.9 → 2). Explicit integer validation. F26 docs/RELEASING.md:36 "tests on 3.9/3.12" is stale: CI runs 3.9/3.12/3.13 + macOS 3.12. Update the version list. F27 docs/algorithm.md:351 "recall the factorisation g0 = w' mu with w = V^-1 c" — the w'μ notation is never introduced earlier and g0 appears only here; "recall" points to nothing. Introduce the notation at eqs. (4)/(5) or define inline. F28 docs/assumptions.md:8 "The high-level predictor uses additive genetic sharing only" is true for the default only; c2/m2 add environmental off-diagonals two paragraphs later. Prepend "By default,". F29 docs/inference.md:33-35 The detectable-enrichment formula omits the _CASE_RATE_RATIO_TOL = 1.15 floor (fit.py:165): for K = 0.05 and n ≳ 30,400 the binding threshold is 1.15×, not the formula's value. Note the max(formula, 1.15×) floor. F30 benchmarks/RESULTS.md:955 "M 0.17 vs truth 0.15": the hash-matched run log gives 0.163 (rounds to 0.16). §24 is log-only (no CSV, no guard). Fix the digit; consider a CSV for §24. F31 benchmarks/RESULTS.md §26/§27 Stored CIs are normal (1.96×SE) over 3–5 replicates; t-criticals would be 2.2–4.3× wider. F32 .github/workflows/ci.yml:69 Comment says "That is ~285 tests"; actual collection is 297 (verified with --collect-only). Update the count or drop the number. F33 docs/algorithm.md:563-566 Quotation marks around a paraphrase of Dybdahl Krebs et al. 2026: the paper says "noisy measures of additive genetic liability", not "noisy estimates of the same additive genetic liability". Quote verbatim or drop the quotation marks. "Public PA implementations include LTFGRS (benchmarked here) and the original PAFGRS package." F35 docs/estimation.md:120-123 The clause that Hujoel et al. 2022 "preferred a logistic combination when clinical covariates were included" could not be verified from the accessible text (publisher full text paywalled). The core claim (PRS+FH combination improves prediction) is verified. Confirm against the paper's STAR Methods or soften the sentence. F36 tests/ (several) Small untested branches: the families_from_columns length-mismatch error; multi-trait var values (smoke-only); gibbs_advance_moment (used by the research MCEM, only indirect coverage); no closed-form oracle for estimation under c2/m2. Extend guards as artifacts are touched; re-pair from replicate rows.

docs.title: 4. The headline claims, assessed
docs.text:
Table 5. Each headline claim of benchmarks/RESULTS.md, traced to its artifact and recomputed. "Supported" means the quoted value and its stated uncertainty reproduce from the committed CSV at quoted precision.

Claim Verdict Note corr(PA, Gibbs) 0.9977–0.9999 across the 27-cell grid Supported Recomputed range 0.997677–0.999900. Stress pedigrees ≥ 0.9984 Not supported (F1) Artifact: worst seed 0.998131, mean 0.998262. Gibbs ≈ LTFHPlus 2.2.0: corr 0.9999, RMSE 0.0041 ± 0.0001 Supported 0.999913 ± 0.000008; 0.004136 ± 0.000116. PA ≈ LTFGRS 1.0.1: corr 1.0000, RMSE 0.000087 ± 0.000008 Supported Recomputed from 3 replicate rows. Fold times 6.87 ± 0.12× / 1178 ± 157×; mixed 6613 ± 800× Reproduces; framing since corrected The values re-derive from the CSV, and the algorithm-mixing caveat ("not 'LT-FH++, but faster'") is right. What this row missed is that the two same-algorithm folds were measured at 4 Numba threads against 1 future worker, and only one of them is thread-sensitive: re-run matched at one thread, LTFHPlus/Gibbs is about 1.8× (not 6.87×) while LTFGRS/PA exceeds 1500×. Recomputing a number from its artifact cannot detect a resource asymmetry in how the artifact was produced; §30 now carries both columns. PA 384–488× faster than grouped Gibbs (4 threads) Supported Thread-count caveat stated. Classic LT-FH NCP ratio 1.47 ± 0.04× Supported for the independent-SNP marginal-association simulation 1.468 ± 0.040 (Gibbs), 1.469 ± 0.039 (PA); no real-LD mixed model. ADuLT 1.049 vs LT-FH++ 1.194; increment +0.1454 ± 0.0154 Supported for the same independent-SNP simulation Independently re-paired from the 10 replicate rows; slope 0.995 ± 0.015. Cohort-blind λ_GC 16.460 ± 0.399 vs cohort-aware 1.007 ± 0.040 Supported Framed as a confounding demonstration, not a method failure — the honest reading. Sex-CIP gap closure 0.05091 ± 0.00096; ΔNCP unresolved (0.0040 ± 0.0046) Digit error (F7); conclusion sound Artifact 0.05092; the unresolved-power statement is appropriately candid. PGS ⊕ LT-FH: R² 0.236 + 0.170 → 0.339; corr 0.2009 ± 0.0046 vs theory 0.2003 ± 0.0050 Supported Consistent with the a·b·√p identity; the doc's stronger verification claim is F12. Mixture max Δcorr −0.00034 ± 0.00011 Supported Detectable but practically negligible — stated as such. IPW ascertainment: ĥ² 0.495 vs truth 0.5 (case/control), 0.473 (enriched) Supported 0.4945 recomputed; positivity and efficiency limits disclosed.

Two interpretation remarks. First, the effect sizes are reported with the right uncertainty almost everywhere — Monte-Carlo SEs for simulation means, paired intervals for few-replicate contrasts — and the document repeatedly warns against substituting one for the other (§5's SD/MC-SE ratio discussion is exemplary). Second, the claims most at risk of over-reading are precisely the ones this review flags: a stale superlative (F1) and unguarded transcriptions (F7, F8, F17). The guard system works; these fell through its gaps.

docs.title: 5. Limitations of this review
docs.text:
1. No benchmark was re-run end to end; claims were verified by recomputation from the committed artifacts and provenance files. The R locks in particular were not re-executed (F16 covers the implication). This is a structural blind spot, not merely an economy: recomputation establishes that a number follows from its artifact, and is silent on whether the experiment behind the artifact was like-for-like. The fold-time row of Table 5 is the worked example — 6.87 ± 0.12× re-derives exactly and was still not the implementation comparison its label promised, because ltpred ran on four threads and the R packages on one worker. Comparability has to be audited by re-running under matched conditions, which is what bench_ltfhplus_compare_1thread.csv now does.
  2. The research/ package was reviewed at the level of its tests and public contracts, not by a full theoretical audit of its EM/MCEM derivations.
  3. Literature verification used the publisher records accessible on 2026-08-16; one sub-clause (F35) could not be confirmed from accessible text and is flagged rather than asserted false.
  4. Numerical probes were run on one machine and one stack (Table 1); nothing here speaks to Windows or to NumPy/SciPy floors beyond what CI covers.

docs.title: 6. Summary
docs.text: The statistical core is correct, the numerics are verified against independent references, the test oracles are sound, the evidence discipline is real, and the literature framing is fair. The two T1 findings are narrow: one stale headline number contradicted by its own artifact (F1), and one vacuous research test (F2). The T2 findings cluster in three places: silent-failure modes at input boundaries (F3–F6), transcription and provenance gaps in the unguarded prose of the evidence ledger (F7–F12), and CI coverage short of the declared support matrix (F13–F16). All are individually small; together they are the natural next hardening pass for a project whose own guard philosophy — "claims carry their evidence" — most of these findings simply extend.

docs.title: Independent review of ltpred v0.4.2 (2026-08-28)
docs.text: A read-only, peer-review-style audit of the statistical core, the estimation and fitting APIs, the supporting numerics, the test and CI machinery, the benchmark evidence base, and the documentation. This review covers the tree at commit 7806e55 (v0.4.2 plus its unreleased changelog entries); it follows, and is independent of, the v0.3.4 audit in REVIEW_2026-08.md. The tier-3 findings it reports were fixed in the same change set that adds this document (section 4 lists the dispositions; see the CHANGELOG for the release entries).

docs.title: 1. Scope and method
docs.text:
The review proceeded in three stages. First, the project's own gates were run: the full test suite, the linter, the benchmark-evidence guard, and the example scripts (Table 1). Second, the statistical core was audited against primary sources and closed forms: the liability-threshold covariance assembly, the Pearson-Aitken selection update and the PA-FGRS censored-control mixture (Dybdahl Krebs et al. 2024, supp. eqs. S3-S5), the truncated-MVN Gibbs conditionals (Kotecha & Djuric 1999), the Kaplan-Meier and Aalen-Johansen cumulative-incidence estimators (Andersen, Borgan, Gill & Keiding 1993; the cmprsk::cuminc finite-risk-set variance), the tetrachoric MLE, the Haseman-Elston variance-component fixed point, and the threshold/CIP conversions. Third, every headline claim was re-verified independently: the numerics in section 3 were recomputed from closed forms, textbook examples, or simulation ground truth rather than taken from the package's own tests. Severity tiers: T1, correctness or scientific validity; T2, robustness, evidence integrity, or maintainability; T3, style, clarity, or polish.

Table 1. Baseline checks run on the review machine (macOS, Apple silicon, arm64; repo venv: CPython 3.10.20, NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.3, Numba 0.67.0, pytest 9.1.1; BLAS threads pinned to one as in CI).

Check Command Result Test suite pytest -q 578 passed, 56 s Lint ruff check . clean Evidence guards scripts/check_evidence.py all benchmark claims internally consistent Examples examples/vignette.py runs end to end (the other two example scripts are exercised by CI, not re-run here)

docs.title: 2. Verdicts by area
docs.text:
Statistical core (covariance.py, thresholds.py, pearson_aitken.py, gibbs.py). Correct. The role-grammar shared-DNA fractions (parents, sibs, grandparents, half-sibs, avuncular, children across partner groups) were checked pair by pair; the tabular-method kinship computer (Henderson 1976) was checked on hand-built pedigrees including a first-cousin pair and a sib-mating inbreeding loop (A[i,i] = 1.25); the positive-definite nudge was checked on singular and indefinite matrices. The bound conventions (case above threshold, onset pins, censored controls), the -ppf(p) tail-safe quantiles, the log-CDF far-tail expansions, and the far-right-tail truncated-normal sampler and moments were all verified against high-precision references. The PA sequential update is exactly the classical rank-1 selection update, and its active-leading-block optimisation was verified algebraically (coordinates already folded never re-enter the target's moments).

Estimation (estimate.py). Correct. The Pearson-Aitken fold order is canonicalised (sorted roles), so results are a property of the family structure, not of input row order; Gibbs keeps caller order because the sweep consumes RNG per coordinate, and per-family in-kernel seeding makes seeded results independent of prange scheduling. The collapsed (Rao-Blackwellised) genetic rows agree with the full chain and with closed forms (section 3). The batch-means Monte-Carlo SE (R batchmeans::bmmat convention) and the posterior variance are kept as two distinct quantities, and both are reported with the right caveats. The multi-trait covariance assembler was verified block by block against hand computation, including the same-individual cross-trait entries and the PSD coherence checks on full_corrmat - D genetic_corrmat D.

Fitting (fit.py). Sound, with a deliberately defensive sampling contract. The pooled Haseman-Elston fixed point rejects personalised or onset-pinned bounds (outside its common-threshold estimating contract), tests each role's observed case rate against the prevalence the thresholds assert (binomial z; Kish effective n under IPW), rejects pid-overlapping families, and warns on unascertained use without an explicit sampling=. The ascertainment guard was verified to fire on a case-enriched cohort, where the fitter would otherwise silently pin h2 at 1.0. The h2_se output is honestly described as a within-dataset Monte-Carlo diagnostic, not an inferential SE.

CIP estimation (cip.py). Correct. The risk-set convention (entry < t <= exit), the product-limit and Aalen-Johansen increments, and the Greenwood and finite-risk-set tie-correct Aalen (1978) variances were checked against textbook hand-computed examples and against an exponential competing-risks ground truth (section 3). Zero-length follow-ups carrying an event are rejected rather than silently corrupting a risk set.

Diagnostics and conversions (tetrachoric.py, liability_scale.py). Correct. The tetrachoric MLE recovers a known latent correlation on simulated data; the Lee et al. (2011) observed-to-liability factors and the Lee-Wray null subtraction are stated with the right unit caveats (residual probit scale vs fraction of total liability).

Simulation (simulate.py). Coherent. The age-aware generator's threshold-crossing onset model is exactly invertible against the threshold helpers, and the onset-resolution (register grid) handling converts point pins into the correct two-sided liability intervals. Generation gaps keep parents older than their probands.

Tests, CI, benchmarks, docs. Strong. The suite pins hand-computed oracles (hard-coded Aalen variances, textbook Kaplan-Meier values), and the CI matrix covers Python 3.9-3.14t plus macOS, the no-Numba pure-Python fallback, the declared dependency floors, every example script, and a wheel install away from the source tree. Benchmarks are provenance-marked historical snapshots whose claims a CI guard recomputes from the committed CSVs. The docs and the README distinguish what each comparison does and does not validate (in particular, that the PA-Gibbs agreement checks do not validate the PA-only censoring mixture).

docs.title: 3. Independent verification
docs.text:
Table 2. Checks re-derived for this review, independent of the package's own tests. All passed.

Check Result PA exactness for a single truncation (case and control) matches closed-form truncated-moment conditionals to 1e-10 PA-FGRS censored-control mixture matches a hand-derived version of the paper's supp. eqs. S3-S5 (split at the lifetime threshold, future-case component on (thr_pop, inf)) PA vs Gibbs, age-aware no-mixture families corr 0.99923, RMSE 0.0054 Estimator calibration vs simulated truth (n = 2000, five designs) bias ~1 SE of zero in every design; law-of-total-variance identity Var(mu) + E[var] = 0.4938 vs h2 = 0.5 Collapsed vs full-chain Gibbs agree; both match the closed form E[g | two case parents] kinship_from_pedigree parent-offspring 0.5, full sib 0.5, half-sib 0.25, first cousin 0.125, sib-mating diagonal 1.25 Tetrachoric MLE rho = 0.503 vs true 0.5 (n = 100k simulated pairs) fit_heritability h2 = 0.507 vs true 0.5 on population-sampled families; ascertainment guard raises on case-enriched input Aalen-Johansen CIP vs exponential competing-risks theory 0.5089 vs 0.5160 at age 40; KM above AJ as expected Age -> threshold -> liability round trip exact for lifetime cases; below-threshold liabilities map to NaN onset as documented

docs.title: 4. Findings and dispositions
docs.text:
No T1 or T2 findings.

  • T3-1 tetrachoric_table accepted fractional cell counts silently (e.g. 10.5 cases). Fixed: counts are now required to be nonnegative integers; integral floats such as 5.0 remain accepted, with a regression test.
  • T3-2 correct_positive_definite performed correction_limit + 1 corrections because the loop bound was n <= correction_limit, disagreeing with its documented contract. Fixed: the bound is now n < correction_limit, so the limit is the number of attempts; a limit of 0 rejects an unrepaired matrix, with a regression test.
  • T3-3 Seeding rtmvnorm_gibbs mutates the process-global NumPy RNG, so two concurrent seeded calls to the low-level sampler can interfere. The high-level estimators are unaffected (per-family in-kernel seeding). Documented on the seed parameter; no code change needed.
  • T3-4 The per-family Gibbs seed blocks wrap modulo 2^32, so n * max_rounds > 2^32 (beyond ~43M families per call at the default max_rounds) could collide two families' streams. Documented in _base_seeds; no code change needed.
  • T3-5 _AGE_RANGES / _age_range in ltpred.simulate were dead code kept only because a test pinned the role-stem parsing bug through them. Fixed: removed from the package; the regression pin now lives in the test suite and exercises _role_stem, which _draw_ages actually uses.

docs.title: 5. Second pass: the review branch itself
docs.text:
The branch carrying the section-4 dispositions (review/2026-09, commits 6885132 and 2000857) was then reviewed with the same method, and the two declared gaps of the first pass were closed: the documentation site was built locally under mkdocs build --strict in a fresh venv (clean; the new review page renders in the nav with its tables intact), the evidence guard was run in that same venv (mirroring the CI docs job), and the remaining two example scripts were run end to end (ltfh_power_demo.py: PA–Gibbs agreement 0.9997; registry_pipeline.py: 0.9999). The equations of docs/algorithm.md were checked line by line against the code (the precision-form Gibbs conditionals, the inverse-CDF sweep, the PA rank-1 update, the collapse variance identity, and the mixture weight all match). Every exported name was confirmed to render in the built API page via the per-module mkdocstrings directives.

Table 3. Second-pass independent checks. All passed.

Check Result Multi-trait Gibbs vs 2-D quadrature closed form (one relative observed on two correlated traits) 0.3942 closed form vs 0.3964 Gibbs (within MC error); end-to-end estimate_liability 0.3939; per-trait column alignment correct Zero cross-trait correlation: multi-trait vs single-trait estimates corr 0.99996, max abs diff 0.008 Lee (2011) observed-to-liability factors match hand computation to 1e-12 (K = 0.01 multiplier 13.94); ascertainment factor and round trip exact Tetrachoric SE calibration (300 simulated tables) empirical SD 0.0607 vs mean reported SE 0.0586; bias +0.0003 families_from_columns multi-trait input and broadcast guards works; scalar bounds on the multi-trait path and vector bounds on the single-trait path both rejected with clear messages

Two findings. T3-6 (a defect in the first pass's own T3-1 fix): the fractional-count gate ran math.floor before any finiteness check, so an infinite count raised a bare OverflowError instead of a ValueError (on main such input was caught only incidentally, downstream, by the monomorphism check). Fixed: a finiteness gate now precedes the integer gate; nan and inf counts raise a clean ValueError, with a regression test. T3-7 (observation, no action): the estimator's collapsed-kernel Gibbs reports a Monte-Carlo SE about an order of magnitude smaller than offline batch_means on raw rtmvnorm_gibbs draws for the same draw count, because the collapsed kernel streams the Rao-Blackwellised conditional mean rather than raw g draws. This is by design and is documented in docs/algorithm.md step G2; it is recorded here so a cross-check against the low-level sampler is not misread as a bug.

docs.title: 6. What this review did not do
docs.text: The R-package lock comparisons (LTFHPlus 2.2.0, LTFGRS 1.0.1) and the HAPNEST real-LD benchmark path were not re-run (they need R and external genotype data); their stored artifacts were checked for internal consistency by scripts/check_evidence.py instead. The full benchmark suite was not re-run (the provenance note in benchmarks/RESULTS.md already records the snapshot procedure). The documentation site was rebuilt locally in the second pass, as recorded in section 5; it was not deployed from the review branch.

docs.title: Independent review of ltpred v0.5.1 (2026-09-02)
docs.text: A read-only audit of what changed since the v0.4.2 review, plus the two installed modules that neither previous review examined. This review covers the tree at commit a6b18be (v0.5.1). It follows, and is independent of, the v0.3.4 audit in REVIEW_2026-08.md and the v0.4.2 audit in REVIEW_2026-09.md. No package code was changed by the review; the only edits are this document and its mkdocs.yml nav entry.

docs.title: 1. Scope and method
docs.text:
The statistical core (covariance.py, thresholds.py, pearson_aitken.py, gibbs.py, estimate.py, fit.py, cip.py, tetrachoric.py, liability_scale.py, simulate.py) was audited twice in the last month against primary sources and closed forms, and its verdicts stand. This review does not repeat that work. It concentrates on the package delta since commit 7806e55 (nine files, +488/-57 lines) and on the two installed modules the earlier reviews did not list: pipeline.py, the public register driver added in 0.5.0, and pedigree.py, whose extraction gained ancestral-closure marking and shortest-degree relaxation in the same release.

Three stages. First, the project's own gates were run (Table 1). Second, the delta was read line by line against the 0.5.0 and 0.5.1 changelog entries and the documentation. Third, every claim that matters was checked independently by execution: alignment contracts, the new kernel path against the role grammar, the direction of the driver's calendar censoring, and two suspected silent-failure modes, each reproduced on a hand-built table (Table 2). Severity tiers as before: T1, correctness or scientific validity; T2, robustness, evidence integrity, or maintainability; T3, style, clarity, or polish.

Table 1. Baseline checks on the review machine (macOS, Apple silicon; repo venv: CPython 3.10.20, NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.3, Numba 0.67.0; BLAS pinned to one thread as in CI).

Check Command Result Test suite pytest -q tests 618 passed, 61 s Lint ruff check . clean Evidence guard scripts/check_evidence.py internally consistent: scaling 392 to 518x; PA stress floor 0.9991; R locks 6.786 +/- 0.079x and 1418 +/- 30x; PGS 0.338 / 0.236 / 0.170 Docs mkdocs build --strict builds; the red text is the Material for MkDocs 2.0 announcement, not a strict-mode warning Example examples/vignette.py runs end to end; register example gives GWAS +1.017439, prediction -0.072034, post-index and closure invariance 0.0

docs.title: 2. Verdicts by area
docs.text:
Register driver (pipeline.py). Correct where it computes; the gaps are at its boundaries. The prediction-mode censoring is right in every case checked: a relative's record after the landmark becomes a control censored at that relative's own attained age, a pre-landmark diagnosis stays a pinned case, a pre-landmark exit stays a control at exit age, and a member born at or after the landmark is uninformative. The proband's own row is made uninformative under use="prediction" and conditioned under use="gwas". The alignment the driver relies on, that kinship_from_pedigree returns the matrix in the order of the ids it was given so that target=0 is the proband, holds: the tabular method iterates in topological order but writes A[i, j] at the original positions (covariance.py:473-540). What the driver does not do is report on the two conditions that most often make a register analysis wrong without making any single score wrong: parent references that failed to resolve, and probands who are not at risk at the landmark (findings T2-1 and T2-2).

Pedigree extraction (pedigree.py). Correct. Ancestral closure includes every recorded ancestor of every extracted member, closure nodes included, so the extracted kinship is the population kinship restricted to the set; the docstring's claim holds and is under test. Shortest-degree relaxation during closure can only lower a degree, and no closure node can end below max_degree because the breadth-first pass already explores parent edges. Sibling edges give half-sibs degree 2 through the shared parent and mates degree 2 through a shared child, as documented.

Kinship-route environmental kernels (covariance.py). Correct. With a sibship kernel over the proband and two full sibs, the kinship route reproduces construct_covmat_single(c2=...) to 0.0 in every entry (Table 2). The kernel does not reach the parents, so Cov(o, m) stays h2/2. Validation is complete: symmetry to 1e-8 then canonicalised, unit diagonal, positive semi-definite to -1e-8, h2 + c2 + m2 <= 1, and a nonzero proportion without its kernel is refused rather than guessed from A.

Threshold helpers and diagnostics. The removal of the pop_prev = 0.1 default from the six public helpers is the right change: a package cannot carry a disease-independent prevalence. thresholds_from_cip documents that k_pop defaults to max(cip_values) and clips a young control's CIP at min_cip = 1e-5, which is what keeps a disease-free two-year-old uninformative without an infinite bound. The tetrachoric finiteness gate now precedes the integer gate, closing T3-6 of the previous review.

Documentation and changelog. Accurate against the code for the delta. Every 0.5.0 entry that names behaviour was found in the code, and the vignette's register example reproduces the invariances it claims.

docs.title: 3. Independent verification
docs.text:
Table 2. Checks re-derived for this review, independent of the package's own tests.

Check Result kinship_from_pedigree row order matrix returned in input order; the driver's target=0 is the proband Kinship-route sibship kernel vs role grammar (o, m, f, s1, s2; h2 = 0.5, c2 = 0.15) max abs difference 0.0; Cov(o, s1) = 0.40 = h2/2 + c2; Cov(o, m) = 0.25 = h2/2 Direction of calendar censoring (father disease-free at 35, 45, 55, 65, 75 at the 2020 landmark) estimate -0.0547, -0.0640, -0.0754, -0.0850, -0.0932: monotone, older disease-free relatives pull the proband down Post-index and closure-only invariance 0.0 in the test suite and in the vignette example Closure relaxation and exact kinship covered by test_degree_is_the_shortest_route_not_the_first_found and test_extraction_preserves_full_pedigree_kinship Silent founder coercion (T2-1) same trio table with parent ids in a different format: estimate +0.3246 with 2 relatives becomes -0.0220 with 0 relatives; no warning, no count Missing landmark eligibility (T2-2) proband diagnosed 2015, landmark 2020, use="prediction": scored +0.3591, no warning, no field; proband exited follow-up 2010: same

docs.title: 4. Findings
docs.text:
No T1 findings. Every score the package computes was correct for the inputs it was given. The T2 findings are about what the register driver does not tell its caller.

T2-1. Unresolved parent references become founders silently. pedigree.py:109-112 and covariance.py:504-508 map any parent value that is not among ids to the founder sentinel -1. That is documented in both docstrings and tested (test_founder_columns_and_ordering), and at the register boundary it is unavoidable: a parent born before the register started is a founder. But the same rule absorbs an id-format mismatch, a failed join, or a truncated column, and in the register driver that turns every family-history score into an own-status-only score with nothing to show for it except a low n_relatives. The reproduction in Table 2 is the whole failure: 2 relatives to 0, no warning. Recommendation: count non-null parent references that did not resolve, once per table in build_parent_graph (ParentGraph.n_unresolved_parents), and surface the fraction of records with at least one unresolved non-null parent on PopulationScores. Warn when that fraction is implausible for a register boundary, and refuse when the resolved fraction is zero with non-null references present, which cannot be a boundary effect. A cheap companion check is dtype: all ids integers and all parent references strings is a certain mismatch.

T2-2. use="prediction" scores probands who are not at risk at the landmark, without saying so. The only proband-level check is that the landmark does not precede birth (pipeline.py:193-199). A proband already diagnosed before index_time, or already out of follow-up, is scored like any other and PopulationScores carries no field that distinguishes them. The vignette is honest that the driver "does not construct an eligible incident-risk cohort" (line 757), so this is a documented boundary. It is still the wrong place to leave it. The driver already holds record_time[proband] and index_time, and including prevalent cases in a prospective evaluation is exactly the cohort-level leakage the use= design exists to prevent: their family histories are enriched, so discrimination is inflated. Recommendation: return a per-proband state, disease_free_and_followed, prevalent_case, or exited_before_index, and warn when any proband is a prevalent case. Do not raise; a caller may want the scores for a different purpose.

T2-3. A supported driver whose payoff evidence is marked stale. docs/api.md calls estimate_liabilities a supported public API. The evidence that would say what it buys, RESULTS.md section 20 (pedigree payoff) and section 21 (end-to-end register pipeline), is labelled "Historical/stale evidence (2026-08-30)" by the project itself, and ROADMAP item 4 schedules the rerun. The graduation rule's clause for thin orchestration was applied, and the exact-equivalence and invariance tests it asks for exist. But the module docstring calls the glue "small but consequential", and calendar censoring and observation-set choice are consequential. Recommendation: regenerate sections 20 and 21 under the provenance wrapper before the first release (ROADMAP item 7), or until then label the driver in api.md and the vignette as supported with its payoff unquantified.

T3-1. Name the prediction estimand. Under use="prediction" the proband's own row is made uninformative (pipeline.py:264), so the estimand is E[g | relatives observed at the landmark], not E[g | relatives, proband disease-free at the landmark]. That matches the LT-FH prediction and PA-FGRS convention of leaving own status out, and the docstring says the row is left uninformative. It does not say that the second estimand exists or how it differs: for a landmark cohort of mixed ages the two agree on ranking within an age but not on level across ages, since survival to an older age disease-free is evidence of lower liability. One sentence in api.md and the vignette's landmark section would close it.

docs.title: 5. What this review did not do
docs.text: It did not re-derive the statistical core; two reviews in the preceding month did, and nothing in the 0.5.x delta touches the PA update, the Gibbs conditionals, the CIP estimators, or the fitters. It did not re-run the R lock comparisons, the HAPNEST path, or the benchmark suite; the evidence guard was run instead, and the register-benchmark staleness in T2-3 is the project's own label, not a recomputation. It did not read research/. The numerical probes were run on one machine and one stack (Table 1).

docs.title: Independent review of ltpred v0.6.2 (2026-09-10)
docs.text: A read-only audit of the 0.6.0 inference delta. This review covers the tree at commit e9bfa66 (v0.6.2). It follows, and is independent of, the v0.3.4 audit in REVIEW_2026-08.md, the v0.4.2 audit in REVIEW_2026-09.md, and the v0.5.1 audit in REVIEW_2026-09b.md. The audit itself changed no package code; the T1-1 and T2-1 findings it reports were then fixed in the same change set that adds this document, and T3-1 was withdrawn after the validation study it asked for failed to reproduce it (section 4 records the dispositions, including two corrections to the T1-1 measurements found while fixing it; see the CHANGELOG for the release entry).

docs.title: 1. Scope and method
docs.text:
The previous three audits covered the statistical core and the register driver through v0.5.1. Version 0.6.0 added an inference engine and a fitter, and deliberately changed some existing scores:

  • quadrature.py, a new opt-in engine that integrates at most two parental factors for additive nuclear families;
  • pairwise.py (fit_pairwise), a new A/C/M composite-likelihood fitter;
  • _selected_kinship.py, bounded memoized selected relationship entries, used by the register driver behind a new covariance-reduction guard;
  • pearson_aitken.py, where no-mixture PA now conditions all pins jointly and marginalizes uninformative rows before folding intervals — a stated, deliberate change to some pinned-family scores.

This review concentrates on that delta. It does not re-derive the liability model, the covariance construction, the Gibbs conditionals, or the existing fitters; three audits in the preceding six weeks did, and nothing in the delta alters them.

Two stages. First, the project's own gates were run (Table 1). Second, every claim that matters was re-derived by execution against oracles written for this review, not by the package: a dense linear-Gaussian conditioning plus 1-D quadrature oracle for posterior moments (exact for at most two non-pin intervals), a Monte-Carlo oracle drawn directly from the model definition (Sigma = h2 A + (1 - h2) I) with exact pin conditioning, and direct numerical integration of the bivariate normal for the pairwise cell probabilities. Severity tiers as before: T1, correctness or scientific validity; T2, robustness, evidence integrity, or maintainability; T3, style, clarity, or polish.

Table 1. Baseline checks on the review machine (macOS, Apple silicon; repo venv: CPython 3.10.20, NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.3, Numba 0.67.0; BLAS pinned to one thread as in CI).

Check Command Result Test suite pytest -q 800 passed, 60 s Lint ruff check . clean Evidence guard scripts/check_evidence.py internally consistent: scaling 392–518×; PA stress floor 0.9991; IPW 0.468/0.521; R locks 6.786 ± 0.079× and 1418 ± 30×; PGS 0.338 / 0.236 / 0.170; time/memory 7 matched cases; PDF v0.6.2 Documented quadrature example docs/estimation.md snippet, verbatim runs; est 1.036112, var 0.229013, error 1.13e-14, 64 nodes Example script examples/vignette.py runs end to end; GWAS +1.013217, prediction −0.072034, post-index and closure invariance 0.0

docs.title: 2. Verdicts by area
docs.text:
Quadrature engine (quadrature.py). The mathematics is correct and the answers are accurate to floating-point; the mode-finding step has a hard failure mode that makes the engine unusable on a few percent of ordinary inputs. Every reduction was checked by hand and by execution. The analytic branches are right: a proband pinned under out="full" returns the pin with zero variance; h2 = 0 returns the prior; the parents-only branch returns 0.5 h2 E[l_m | interval] for the genetic target and h2 - 0.25 h2² (1 - v) for its variance, both of which follow from the covariance algebra (Var(g_o | l_m in I) = 0.25 Var(g_m | I) + 0.25 h2 + 0.5 h2); and the one-remaining-interval branch is the exact bivariate truncated-normal formula. The Newton mode search is right too: at the returned iterate the gradient vanishes to 1e-17 and the returned Hessian matches a finite-difference Hessian of the same objective (Table 2), so my initial suspicion of a sign error in the (noise - v) / noise² term was wrong — it is the correct (1 - dt/dm) / s² with dt/dm = v/s². The importance-weighted tensor grid is a consistent self-normalized estimator with a valid proposal. End to end, the estimator is exact to ~1e-15 against the dense oracle on every reduction it claims to close, and consistent with independent Monte Carlo on the general multi-interval case (mean z = +0.14, sd 0.87, no |z| > 3 in 78 runs). The defect is not in the arithmetic but in the stopping rule (finding T1-1).

PA pin conditioning (pearson_aitken.py). Correct. Where the result is claimed exact it is exact: all-pins, pin plus one interval, and pins plus two intervals all reproduce the dense oracle to 0.0 or 1e-17 (Table 2). The deliberate score change is real and is visible in the example script: the vignette's GWAS score moved from +1.017439 (v0.5.1) to +1.013217, while the prediction-mode score is unchanged at −0.072034, which is what one expects from conditioning pins jointly before the interval fold.

Pairwise fitter (pairwise.py). Correct. The four cell probabilities match independent bivariate integration to 1.8e-16 over t in [−0.7, 4] and rho in [0.01, 0.99]; the first and second derivatives match Richardson-extrapolated finite differences (5e-9 and 7.6e-10 relative), which matters because the optimizer consumes them as analytic scores. The composite likelihood, the cluster-robust sandwich, and the KKT re-check are standard and are used consistently on a per-family scale. In a recovery experiment I ran independently — 40 replicates of 3,000 simulated five-member families with known A = 0.30, C = 0.15, M = 0.10 — all three components were recovered with well-scaled uncertainty (Table 3). This is new evidence for a fitter whose changelog entry says efficiency and coverage "still require broader validation"; one small caveat is recorded as T3-1.

Selected kinship and the register driver. Correct. _SelectedKinship reproduces kinship_from_pedigree exactly for full pedigrees, random subsets, and caches of 0 through 100,000 entries, including inbred pedigrees (the full-sib-mating child gets the correct diagonal 1.25) and deliberate self-mating. The bound in _covariance_reduction_is_safe is sound: over three structures and ten values of h2, whenever it claimed safety the selected path was bit-identical to the legacy full-matrix path, and its claimed eigenvalue lower bound was never violated (worst sampled margin 20.9×); it correctly defers at h2 <= 1e-6 and at h2 = 1. The two boundary diagnostics added in 0.5.2 in response to the previous review behave as documented: an all-unresolved parent column and an integer-id/string-parent mismatch both raise, a 20% unresolved share scores silently, and proband_state classifies all three proband states while leaving every score unchanged.

Method dispatch and model boundaries. Correct and never silent. A requested method="quadrature" is refused rather than quietly downgraded for multi-trait input, nonzero c2/m2, the mixture, h2 = 1, and arbitrary kinship matrices.

docs.text:
Table 2. Checks re-derived for this review, independent of the package's own tests. "Oracle" is the dense Gaussian-conditioning reference written for this review.

No fit failed and none was discarded, at any size. Weighted least squares on bias(N) = b0 + b1/N puts the asymptotic bias b0 at +0.00005 for A (95% CI −0.00113 to +0.00123), +0.00020 for C (−0.00066 to +0.00107) and +0.00024 for M (−0.00099 to +0.00147), all centred within 0.0002 of zero, with the whole signal in the 1/N term (b1 of −4.67, −1.57 and −3.96; chi2/df 0.42 to 1.21, p 0.30 to 0.74). This study is committed as benchmarks/bench_pairwise_recovery.py, with its numbers in benchmarks/bench_pairwise_recovery.csv, section 32 of benchmarks/RESULTS.md, and a provenance row in benchmarks/run_manifest.jsonl. It reuses the repository's own simulate_families_components: the review's first scratch harness was found to construct the same covariance and was therefore a duplicate. That first harness was run independently and agrees with the committed campaign at every size (largest discrepancy 2.1 SE, at N = 1,500).

docs.title: 4. Findings
docs.text:
T1-1. method="quadrature" refuses ordinary inputs because the mode-search stopping rule sits below the floating-point noise floor. This is the one finding that changes what a user can do; everything else in the delta held up.

_mode (quadrature.py:135) stops when max|step| <= 1e-10 * (1 + max|x|). On affected inputs the Newton iterate reaches the true optimum at the second iteration and then cannot shrink its step below roughly 3e-10, so the test can never pass, the loop runs out its 80 iterations, and the estimator raises. Instrumenting the real code path shows the mechanism exactly: from iteration 2 to iteration 79 the objective is bit-identical (0.459686633802) and x equals SciPy's minimizer to eight decimals, while |step| stalls at 2.8e-10 against a tolerance of 1.13e-10; the Armijo line search accepts only scales of 1e-8 to 1e-7 because the predicted decrease gradient @ step is roundoff. The reproducibility is exact:

from ltpred.quadrature import estimate_liability_quadrature_arrays as est
est(["o", "m", "f"], [[-1.324, -1.238, -1.508]], [[0.796, 1.200, 0.958]], h2=0.5)
# RuntimeError: family 0: quadrature posterior-mode iteration did not converge

Three properties make this T1 rather than a nuisance. First, the failure rate on plausible input is not negligible: 48 of 720 randomized bound sets (6.7%), broken down as 7.5% for two-sided intervals, 9.2% for one-sided population bounds, and 3.3% for the classic LT-FH++ encoding with a pinned proband — the regime the engine is advertised for. Second, no public control rescues an affected family: quadrature_atol and quadrature_max_nodes do not reach _mode, and every combination tried (atol from 1e-8 to 1e-2, max_nodes 128 and 512) still raised on all 16 two-sided refusals sampled. Third, because the estimator raises on the first failing family, the method is unusable at cohort scale: a batch of 50 realistic families raised at family 30, and a batch of 1,000 raised at family 0. The error text also misdescribes the cause — the mode iteration did converge.

The code already contains the intended tolerance for this situation in the line-search else branch, whose comment reads "At floating-point resolution the objective may stop changing before the derivative. This point remains a valid importance proposal; quadrature refinement still determines acceptance." That branch is unreachable here, because the line search does find a (tiny) scale. Recommendation: make the stopping rule noise-aware — accept when the objective stops changing at representable resolution, or when the accepted line-search scale falls below a threshold, or relax the tolerance to the gradient's resolution (about 1e-8 * (1 + max|x|)) — and treat the mode as a proposal rather than a result, which is what the importance reweighting already does. A randomized bound test alongside the existing hand-picked cases would have caught this; tests/test_quadrature.py currently uses only round-number bounds. The refinement diagnostic did not mask the problem, because the estimator raises rather than returning a value.

Two corrections to the measurements above, from re-running them while fixing the defect. The incidence is environment-dependent, because the noise floor of the exact gradient follows SciPy's truncated-moment accuracy: on identical inputs the two-sided/one-sided refusal rates are 6.2%/9.6% under NumPy 1.26 with SciPy 1.15 but 2.1%/4.2% under NumPy 2.4 with SciPy 1.18, and the minimal reproduction above returns rather than raising on the latter. The defect is present in both; only which families trip it changes. Second, the stall is sharper than "the line search accepts tiny scales": the accepted step changes the objective by exactly zero, because scale * step (about 1e-8 x 5e-9) falls below an ulp of x, so candidate equals x bit-for-bit and the Armijo threshold underflows to value. The iterate therefore cannot move at all, rather than moving slowly.

Disposition: fixed. _mode now also returns when an accepted line-search step fails to change the objective at representable resolution (value - candidate_value <= 8 * eps * (1 + |value|)) — the tolerance the else branch already documented but could not reach. The Newton decrement gradient @ step was measured as the more principled alternative and rejected on evidence: across 700 traces its stalled values (up to 2.9e-15) overlap the smallest values seen on genuinely productive iterations (down to 6.4e-20), so no threshold separates the two states.

Validation. Over 1,200 randomized families spanning four role sets, six bound styles, six h2 values and both out modes, mode refusals fall from 49 to 0 and no family that previously returned now raises: the 1,031 answered before are a subset of the 1,076 answered after, 775 of them bit-identical and the rest differing by at most 8.8e-14 in est and 3.0e-13 in var, against the method's own 1e-8 criterion. Four rescued families are genuinely node-limited and now raise the refinement message instead, which max_nodes=128 resolves — an actionable refusal in place of an unrescuable one. On nine previously refused inputs both moments reproduce an independently written 800x800 Gauss-Legendre integration over the two parental breeding values to within 2.0e-15 (est) and 8.9e-16 (var), the oracle being self-consistent to 1e-16 under order doubling, and agree with 40M-draw rejection sampling (max |z| = 1.8). Two regression tests were added: one pins the four verified answers, the other supplies the randomized bound coverage whose absence let this through. Seven of the eight new test cases fail on the pre-fix tree, and the suite (808 tests) passes under both dependency sets above.

T2-1. The node-refinement refusal reports a change that already satisfies the criterion. The convergence test requires two consecutive refinements within atol, but the failure message prints only the last one:

quadrature did not converge by 128 nodes per dimension (last change 7.48e-14, atol 1e-08)

Here the last change is one hundred million times smaller than the tolerance, so the message reads as a contradiction; the actual reason is that the previous refinement exceeded atol. Separately, with the default max_nodes=128 only three refinement comparisons exist (16→32→64→128), so a family that stabilizes at 256 nodes is refused; that case is rescued by max_nodes=512 (error 7.5e-14 at 256 nodes), but the message does not mention the knob. Recommendation: report max(changes[-2:]) and name the refinement that failed, and mention quadrature_max_nodes in the message.

Disposition: fixed. The refusal now reports max(changes[-2:]), the quantity the criterion actually tests, worded as "largest of the last two changes". Re-measuring while fixing it relocated the binding case: it is max_nodes=64, the documented minimum, where the ladder 16→32→64 leaves only two changes and so forces the coarse first refinement into the acceptance test. A deep-tail family at h2=0.95 refused with changes = [7.76e-06, 9.58e-09] while reporting only 9.58e-09 — and that same family returns at max_nodes=128 carrying error equal to 9.58e-09, the very number the refusal had quoted. The two-successive-refinements rule is documented behaviour and was left alone; only the message changed, plus two sentences in docs/estimation.md recording that both changes must pass and that raising quadrature_max_nodes is the remedy.

T3-1. WITHDRAWN. The reported negative bias in the A component of fit_pairwise was an artifact of using 40 replicates. The finding as first written read: mean A of 0.284 against a truth of 0.300, about −0.37 empirical SD with a nominal t near −2.4, offered as an observation for a validation study to pursue. The validation study was run (Table 4) and does not reproduce it.

At the identical design and cohort size, 2,933 replicates give a bias in A of −0.0011 ± 0.0009 — indistinguishable from zero and fourteen times smaller than the −0.0159 first reported. The original design was replicated faithfully: the sampling SDs of Table 3 agree with those of the large study to within 0.7 standard errors of an SD from 40 draws. What was not adequate was the number of replicates. Forty draws put SE(mean) at 0.0068 for A, so the reported deviation was a 2.3 SE fluctuation of the review's own mean; the C deviation was +2.5 SE in the opposite direction. Two further facts complete the account. Three components were examined, and the probability that at least one shows |t| > 2.3 by chance is 0.06. And Â and Ĉ are negatively correlated across replicates, at −0.54 to −0.63, so a single under-powered replicate set tends to show exactly the observed signature of A low with C high.

The mechanism the finding proposed was also wrong on theory, independently of the numbers. It suggested that ignoring within-family dependence beyond the cluster sandwich would bias the additive component. It does not: a pairwise composite likelihood with correctly specified bivariate margins is consistent whatever the dependence among pairs, which costs efficiency and corrupts naive variance estimates but not consistency. There is a real intrinsic bias in this estimator, and it is negative, but it is O(1/N) and far too small to see here. In the one-component, one-pair-per-family design at threshold zero the composite MLE is exactly 2 sin(π(p̂ − ½)) in the concordant fraction, which is concave for A > 0 since g''(p) = −π²A; enumerating the binomial sampling distribution gives N × bias → −0.3667, so about −0.0001 at N = 3,000.

Disposition: withdrawn, and the study it asked for is now reported. No defect is demonstrated, and the estimator is consistent here: the asymptotic bias is within 0.0002 of zero for all three components, with confidence intervals no wider than ±0.0013. What remains is a genuine but small negative finite-sample bias of about −4.7/N in A, which is −0.0032 at N = 1,500 — roughly 1% of the parameter — and negligible by N = 6,000. Its sign is the one the concavity argument above predicts, and its coefficient is about thirteen times the reducible case's −0.3667, the direction ten dependent pairs, three components and a 10% case rate should move it. The positive result is the calibration the changelog said was missing: SE/SD between 0.96 and 1.10, coverage between 0.940 and 0.975, no failed or discarded fits in 11,364 replicates, and boundary pinning confined to M — the component nearest zero — falling from 10.3% at N = 1,500 to nil by N = 12,000, with A never pinned. An earlier scratch run had shown the A interval covering 0.926 with SE/SD 0.92 at N = 12,000, flagged then as possibly a small-sample SE effect; the committed campaign gives 0.944 and 0.96 at that size, so it was the expected outlier among fifteen cells and not a property of the estimator.

T3-2. The quadrature documentation could name its practical failure surface. docs/estimation.md correctly states that failure to meet the refinement criterion raises and that no unchecked value is returned. Once T1-1 is fixed it would still help to say that the engine is a cross-check on nuclear-family structures rather than a cohort-scale workhorse, and that refusals are input-dependent rather than rare.

Disposition: partly addressed. The concrete, measured part is now documented (the two-change acceptance rule and the max_nodes remedy, under T2-1). The broader positioning claim was left out: with mode refusals removed, the remaining refusals are the documented refinement criterion doing its job, and characterizing the engine's cohort-scale standing is a judgement for the maintainer rather than a review finding.

docs.title: 5. What this review did not do
docs.text: It did not re-derive the liability model, the covariance construction, the Gibbs conditionals, the CIP estimators, the existing fitters, or the tetrachoric and liability-scale helpers; three audits in the preceding six weeks did, and the delta does not touch them. It did not re-run the benchmark suite, the R lock comparisons, or the HAPNEST path; the evidence guard was run instead, and the 0.6.1 time/memory claims were not recomputed. It did not audit the benchmarks/ or research/ trees. The numerical probes were run on one machine and one stack (Table 1); the quadrature Monte-Carlo comparisons used 2.5–4 million draws, so agreement is established at the 1e-4 level there and at 1e-15 only where a closed-form oracle applies.

docs.title: Documentation and onboarding review of ltpred v0.7.0 (2026-09-21)
docs.text:
A read-only audit of the user-facing surface: the documentation set, the runnable examples, and the simulated data a new user can obtain. This review covers the tree at commit 2722a59 (v0.7.0). It follows, and is independent of, the four preceding audits — v0.3.4 (REVIEW_2026-08.md), v0.4.2 (REVIEW_2026-09.md), v0.5.1 (REVIEW_2026-09b.md) and v0.6.2 (REVIEW_2026-09c.md, at e9bfa66), fifteen commits behind this one.

Those four audits re-derived the statistical core against independent oracles. This one does not, and deliberately so. It examines a surface no previous audit touched: whether a person who installs ltpred can actually learn to use it. Every claim below is either a file/line citation or a measurement I ran; nothing is re-derived from the model, and no numerical finding of the earlier audits is reopened. The audit changed no package code.

Severity tiers follow the chain, re-read for this domain: T1, a user cannot complete a documented task, or a document states something false; T2, significant friction, a broken promise to installed users, or duplication that will drift; T3, clarity and polish.

docs.title: 1. Scope and method
docs.text:
Two questions frame the audit. First: can a reader execute what the documentation shows? Second: can a user obtain simulated data for every supported route? The second question matters more than it looks, because ltpred's whole value proposition is that a user supplies a cohort — and the only way to learn a pipeline that consumes a cohort is to have one.

Method. I read the complete documentation set (twelve pages, 31,730 words) and all four examples. I then ran every copy-paste path a new user is offered: the README quickstart, docs/quickstart.md steps 1–5, the multi-trait recipe in docs/data-preparation.md, and all four examples/*.py. I inventoried the distribution artifacts to establish what an installed user actually receives, and I counted the exported API surface against the documentation. Where a suspicion proved wrong on execution, that is recorded too (§2, §3).

Table 1. Baseline checks on the review machine (macOS arm64; CPython 3.10.20, NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.15.3, Numba 0.66.0; BLAS pinned to one thread as in CI). The repository's own .venv could not be used: its SciPy fails to dlopen (_spropack...so, "zero-fill section type, but offset field is not zero"), a local packaging problem unrelated to ltpred.

Check Command Result Lint ruff check . clean All examples python examples/*.py 4/4 exit 0, 5.2–14.6 s each, empty stderr README quickstart verbatim into a scratch script runs; est/var shape (2000,); se 0; PA vs Gibbs on 200 families corr 0.99946, max abs diff 0.0104 — the claimed "~1e-2" is accurate docs/quickstart.md §1–5 verbatim into a scratch script runs in 1.5 s; [('P1', 1.357058752244415), ('P2', 0.4619554497275081)] data-preparation.md multi-trait recipe verbatim, (n_people, n_traits) bounds runs; families_from_columns accepts 2-D bounds and gives each Member per-trait arrays. I suspected this snippet was wrong; it is not Wheel contents unzip -l dist/ltpred-0.4.0-py3-none-any.whl 22 files, all under ltpred/ Sdist contents tar tzf dist/ltpred-0.4.0.tar.gz ltpred/, README, CHANGELOG, CITATION, LICENSE, MANIFEST.in, PKG-INFO, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg. No docs/, examples/, benchmarks/, tests/, research/ Docs build not re-run CI builds mkdocs build --strict on every push

Nothing here is broken in the sense of failing. Every documented command that claims to run, runs. The findings are about what the documentation set does not offer, and about a gap between the package a user installs and the package the docs describe.

docs.title: 2. What holds up
docs.text:
The documentation is accurate. That is worth stating plainly, because it is the hard part and it is done. I found no false statement. Every number I could re-derive matched: the README's PA/Gibbs agreement claim reproduced at 0.0104 against a claimed "~1e-2"; the quickstart's scores came out of a verbatim transcription; the multi-trait recipe I expected to be a documentation bug is correct, because families_from_columns genuinely accepts per-trait bound columns.

The hedging discipline is a genuine strength and should not be traded away. The distinction between Monte-Carlo error and approximation error (res.se is exactly 0 under PA, "which is not the same as zero approximation error"); the warning that a family-history phenotype can concentrate a birth-cohort trend rather than dilute it (λ = 10.275 with one lifetime K against 4.616 for the raw label); the insistence that use="prediction" hides own diagnosis but does not select a disease-free risk set; the note that the sib tetrachoric estimates h² + 2c² and is not interchangeable with the parent–offspring one — these are exactly the errors a competent analyst makes, and the docs prevent them. Most packages would not think to mention them.

The engineering hygiene is above the norm. CI runs all four examples end to end (.github/workflows/ci.yml, job examples), with a comment recording that they "were previously run by neither the tests nor CI, so they could rot silently". The docs job builds --strict and notes that strict mode still leaves link resolution at INFO. scripts/check_evidence.py reconciles release-defining numbers against committed artifacts. tests/test_vignette.py pins the register example's calendar and closure contracts. The provenance instinct is consistently good.

The information architecture is sound at the page level. index → guide → quickstart → vignette → workflow(5) → reference(4) is a sensible shape, and "choose a method" as a distinct page is the right call for a package where four published method names describe observation models rather than algorithms.

So the problem is not accuracy or rigour. It is genre: the documentation set is written as a contract, and a contract is what a user needs second.

docs.text:
